title: Validation of the WAge Index: an integrated tool for age-inclusive assessment of physical and psychosocial working environments
official: Test-retest reliability, measurement invariance, and usability of a condensed physical and psychosocial workplace assessment instrument (WAge Index) among manufacturing and service workers aged 18–65 across three European countries: a prospective observational validation study
summary:
Background and study aims
The WAge project has developed an integrated model that combines physical factors (such as postures, physical load, and musculoskeletal symptoms) with psychosocial factors (such as job demands, social support, and organisational practices) to assess how workplaces support health across the lifespan. This model was built using data from a first study involving workers in Portugal, Spain, and Poland.
This second study (WAge-S2) aims to test whether a shorter version of the assessment tools used in the first study produces consistent and reliable results when used a second time, whether the model works in the same way across different countries, and whether the tools are practical and easy to use in real workplaces. The ultimate goal is to develop the WAge Index, an age-inclusive tool that organisations can use to assess their working environments and identify areas for improvement.

Who can participate?
Workers aged 18 to 65 years who are employed in manufacturing or service organisations participating in the WAge project in Portugal, Spain, or Poland. Participants must work at least 20 hours per week in their current role and have a correct understanding of the native language. Workers who are pregnant, experiencing acute illness or injury affecting their physical capacity, or absent due to sickness on the day of data collection cannot take part.

What does the study involve?
Participants complete a set of questionnaires about their working conditions, health, and wellbeing on two occasions, approximately 3 to 6 weeks apart. The questionnaires cover physical demands and discomfort, psychosocial aspects of work, and general health and wellbeing. Each session takes approximately 20 to 30 minutes. After completing the second round, participants are invited to give feedback on how easy the questionnaires were to understand and complete and whether the process was practical in their workplace setting. Participation is voluntary and can be withdrawn at any time.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
By taking part, workers contribute to the development of the WAge Index, a new tool designed to help organisations create healthier working environments for people of all ages. There are no known risks associated with participation. All data is handled confidentially and anonymised before being shared for analysis.

Where is the study run from?
The study is coordinated by SINTEF (Oslo, Norway) and is conducted at workplace sites in three countries: Portugal (coordinated by the Faculty of Human Kinetics, University of Lisbon), Spain (coordinated by the Instituto de Biomecánica de Valencia and Universitat Jaume I), and Poland (coordinated by the Central Institute for Labour Protection [CIOP-PIB], Warsaw).

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
May 2026 to February 2027

Who is funding the study?
The study is funded by the European Union through the Horizon Europe programme (Grant Agreement No. 101137207)

Who is the main contact?
Victor Gonzalez, victor.gonzalez@sintef.no

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Currently employed in manufacturing or service sector organisations participating in the WAge project in Portugal, Spain, or Poland
2. Correct understanding of the native language
3. Currently performing their work as their main occupation for at least 20 hours per week
Exclusion criteria:
1. Pregnancy
2. Acute illnesses, accidents, or other health conditions that currently affect physical capacity
3. Sickness absence on the day of the measurements
